full_original_page:
# 841. Continuous densities for inhomogeneous grid projections

**Area:** Geometry and topology
**Status:** 🟡 PARTIAL
**Last checked:** 2026-10-30

## Problem statement

Let $`M\geq2`$ be an integer. Fix weights $`p_{ij}\in[0,1]`$, $`0\leq i,j<M`$, satisfying
```math
S:=\sum_{i,j}p_{ij}>M,\qquad q_{ij}:=p_{ij}/S.
```

For $`T_{ij}(x,y)=((x+i)/M,(y+j)/M)`$, let $`\nu`$ be the unique probability measure on $`[0,1]^2`$ satisfying
```math
\nu=\sum_{i,j}q_{ij}(T_{ij})_*\nu.
```

For $`\theta\in[0,\pi)`$, put $`\pi_\theta(x,y)=x\cos\theta+y\sin\theta`$ and $`\nu_\theta=(\pi_\theta)_*\nu`$.

Does there exist a set $`E\subset[0,\pi)`$, depending on these fixed weights, with $`\dim_H E=0`$, such that every $`\nu_\theta`$, $`\theta\notin E`$, has a **continuous density on $`\mathbb R`$**?

Equivalently, outside $`E`$, seek a nonnegative continuous function $`f_\theta`$, supported on $`I_\theta=\pi_\theta([0,1]^2)`$, zero outside this interval, with $`\int f_\theta=1`$ and
```math
\sum_{i,j}p_{ij}f_\theta(Mt-i\cos\theta-j\sin\theta)
 =\frac{S}{M}f_\theta(t).
```

Continuity is required for each fixed direction; no joint angle regularity or strict positivity throughout $`I_\theta`$ is imposed.

## Application

These weights arise from a recursive random retention model. The question concerns the associated **deterministic** mass distribution and asks how many viewing directions can obstruct continuity of its projected density. Conclusions about intervals in random shadows require additional positivity conditions.

## References

- K. Simon and L. Vágó, *Fractal Percolations*, Banach Center Publications **115** (2018), 183–196, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.4064/bc115-6). [Primary v2](https://arxiv.org/html/1803.11426v2), **Conjecture 4.12**, equations (4.2)–(4.4) and the dimension-greater-than-one regime at the start of §4.
- P. Shmerkin and B. Solomyak, *Absolute continuity of self-similar measures, their projections and convolutions*, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. **368** (2016), 5125–5151, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1090/tran6696), Theorem B.
- K. Simon and L. Vágó, *Projections of Fractal percolation constructed with inhomogeneous probabilities*, [arXiv:1505.05477](https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.05477), **withdrawn 31 October 2016**.

## Status review


**Known cases:** Lq projected densities outside a zero-dimensional exceptional set need not be continuous. Homogeneous-retention results and random-shadow interval results differ from the arbitrary deterministic grid weights. The 2015 inhomogeneous claim was withdrawn and is not used as a resolution.

**Remaining target:** Resolve the full Problem statement with its stated quantifiers and hypotheses; the restricted advances discussed here do not settle that target.

### Online recheck, 2026-10-30

Lq projected densities outside a zero-dimensional exceptional set need not be continuous. Homogeneous-retention results and random-shadow interval results differ from the arbitrary deterministic grid weights. The 2015 inhomogeneous claim was withdrawn and is not used as a resolution.

The primary-source formulation and earlier dated status review are retained below. Fresh query results and hypothesis comparisons are recorded in the [integration register](../research/further-integration-2026-10-30/README.md). This is a bounded literature and announcement search, not a guarantee of continued openness or certification of every cited proof.

**Partial progress; continuity remains open in searches checked 28 October 2026.** The known $`L^q`$-density conclusion, for some $`q>1`$, outside a zero-dimensional exceptional set does not establish continuity. Homogeneous and later equal-retention affine results have narrower hypotheses or concern projected sets.

The earlier 2015 claim was withdrawn because of an error affecting its main theorem; it is not treated as a resolution. The latest eligible source retains Conjecture 4.12. No matching nonwithdrawn complete result, counterexample or announcement was found, and semantic checks against all-status AIM and private entries found no equivalent target.

The condition $`S>M`$ states explicitly the source’s intended dimension-greater-than-one regime; it is not printed in the isolated conjecture sentence. Here $`p_{ij}`$ are retention weights, while $`q_{ij}`$ are probability weights. The eigenvalue is $`S/M`$.
